1→# Shopify App Template - React Router
     2→
     3→This is a template for building a [Shopify app](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/getting-started) using [React Router](https://reactrouter.com/). It was forked from the [Shopify Remix app template](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix) and converted to React Router.
     4→
     5→Rather than cloning this repo, follow the [Quick Start steps](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router#quick-start).
     6→
     7→Visit the [`shopify.dev` documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) for more details on the React Router app package.
     8→
     9→## Upgrading from Remix
    10→
    11→If you have an existing Remix app that you want to upgrade to React Router, please follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/wiki/Upgrading-from-Remix). Otherwise, please follow the quick start guide below.
    12→
    13→## Quick start
    14→
    15→### Prerequisites
    16→
    17→Before you begin, you'll need to [download and install the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/getting-started) if you haven't already.
    18→
    19→### Setup
    20→
    21→```shell
    22→shopify app init --template=https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router
    23→```
    24→
    25→### Local Development
    26→
    27→```shell
    28→shopify app dev
    29→```
    30→
    31→Press P to open the URL to your app. Once you click install, you can start development.
    32→
    33→Local development is powered by [the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli). It logs into your account, connects to an app, provides environment variables, updates remote config, creates a tunnel and provides commands to generate extensions.
    34→
    35→### Authenticating and querying data
    36→
    37→To authenticate and query data you can use the `shopify` const that is exported from `/app/shopify.server.js`:
    38→
    39→```js
    40→export async function loader({ request }) {
    41→  const { admin } = await shopify.authenticate.admin(request);
    42→
    43→  const response = await admin.graphql(`
    44→    {
    45→      products(first: 25) {
    46→        nodes {
    47→          title
    48→          description
    49→        }
    50→      }
    51→    }`);
    52→
    53→  const {
    54→    data: {
    55→      products: { nodes },
    56→    },
    57→  } = await response.json();
    58→
    59→  return nodes;
    60→}
    61→```
    62→
    63→This template comes pre-configured with examples of:
    64→
    65→1. Setting up your Shopify app in [/app/shopify.server.ts](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/shopify.server.ts)
    66→2. Querying data using Graphql. Please see: [/app/routes/app.\_index.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/app._index.tsx).
    67→3. Responding to webhooks. Please see [/app/routes/webhooks.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx).
    68→4. Using metafields, metaobjects, and declarative custom data definitions. Please see [/app/routes/app.\_index.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/app._index.tsx) and [shopify.app.toml](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/shopify.app.toml).
    69→
    70→Please read the [documentation for @shopify/shopify-app-react-router](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) to see what other API's are available.
    71→
    72→## Shopify Dev MCP
    73→
    74→This template is configured with the Shopify Dev MCP. This instructs [Cursor](https://cursor.com/), [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) and [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and [Google Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) to use the Shopify Dev MCP.
    75→
    76→For more information on the Shopify Dev MCP please read [the documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/devmcp).
    77→
    78→## Deployment
    79→
    80→### Application Storage
    81→
    82→This template uses [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io/) to store session data, by default using an [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html) database.
    83→The database is defined as a Prisma schema in `prisma/schema.prisma`.
    84→
    85→This use of SQLite works in production if your app runs as a single instance.
    86→The database that works best for you depends on the data your app needs and how it is queried.
    87→Here’s a short list of databases providers that provide a free tier to get started:
    88→
    89→| Database   | Type             | Hosters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
    90→| ---------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    91→| MySQL      | SQL              | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-mysql), [Planet Scale](https://planetscale.com/), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Google Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql) |
    92→| PostgreSQL | SQL              | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-postgresql), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Google Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres)                                   |
    93→| Redis      | Key-value        | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-redis), [Amazon MemoryDB](https://aws.amazon.com/memorydb/)                                                                                                        |
    94→| MongoDB    | NoSQL / Document | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-mongodb), [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas/database)                                                                                                  |
    95→
    96→To use one of these, you can use a different [datasource provider](https://www.prisma.io/docs/reference/api-reference/prisma-schema-reference#datasource) in your `schema.prisma` file, or a different [SessionStorage adapter package](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-api-js/blob/main/packages/shopify-api/docs/guides/session-storage.md).
    97→
    98→### Build
    99→
   100→Build the app by running the command below with the package manager of your choice:
   101→
   102→Using yarn:
   103→
   104→```shell
   105→yarn build
   106→```
   107→
   108→Using npm:
   109→
   110→```shell
   111→npm run build
   112→```
   113→
   114→Using pnpm:
   115→
   116→```shell
   117→pnpm run build
   118→```
   119→
   120→## Hosting
   121→
   122→When you're ready to set up your app in production, you can follow [our deployment documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment) to host it externally. From there, you have a few options:
   123→
   124→- [Google Cloud Run](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment/deploy-to-google-cloud-run): This tutorial is written specifically for this example repo, and is compatible with the extended steps included in the subsequent [**Build your app**](tutorial) in the **Getting started** docs. It is the most detailed tutorial for taking a React Router-based Shopify app and deploying it to production. It includes configuring permissions and secrets, setting up a production database, and even hosting your apps behind a load balancer across multiple regions.
   125→- [Fly.io](https://fly.io/docs/js/shopify/): Leverages the Fly.io CLI to quickly launch Shopify apps to a single machine.
   126→- [Render](https://render.com/docs/deploy-shopify-app): This tutorial guides you through using Docker to deploy and install apps on a Dev store.
   127→- [Manual deployment guide](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment/deploy-to-hosting-service): This resource provides general guidance on the requirements of deployment including environment variables, secrets, and persistent data.
   128→
   129→When you reach the step for [setting up environment variables](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/deployment/web#set-env-vars), you also need to set the variable `NODE_ENV=production`.
   130→
   131→## Gotchas / Troubleshooting
   132→
   133→### Database tables don't exist
   134→
   135→If you get an error like:
   136→
   137→```
   138→The table `main.Session` does not exist in the current database.
   139→```
   140→
   141→Create the database for Prisma. Run the `setup` script in `package.json` using `npm`, `yarn` or `pnpm`.
   142→
   143→### Navigating/redirecting breaks an embedded app
   144→
   145→Embedded apps must maintain the user session, which can be tricky inside an iFrame. To avoid issues:
   146→
   147→1. Use `Link` from `react-router` or `@shopify/polaris`. Do not use `<a>`.
   148→2. Use `redirect` returned from `authenticate.admin`. Do not use `redirect` from `react-router`
   149→3. Use `useSubmit` from `react-router`.
   150→
   151→This only applies if your app is embedded, which it will be by default.
   152→
   153→### Webhooks: shop-specific webhook subscriptions aren't updated
   154→
   155→If you are registering webhooks in the `afterAuth` hook, using `shopify.registerWebhooks`, you may find that your subscriptions aren't being updated.
   156→
   157→Instead of using the `afterAuth` hook declare app-specific webhooks in the `shopify.app.toml` file. This approach is easier since Shopify will automatically sync changes every time you run `deploy` (e.g: `npm run deploy`). Please read these guides to understand more:
   158→
   159→1. [app-specific vs shop-specific webhooks](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe#app-specific-subscriptions)
   160→2. [Create a subscription tutorial](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe/get-started?deliveryMethod=https)
   161→
   162→If you do need shop-specific webhooks, keep in mind that the package calls `afterAuth` in 2 scenarios:
   163→
   164→- After installing the app
   165→- When an access token expires
   166→
   167→During normal development, the app won't need to re-authenticate most of the time, so shop-specific subscriptions aren't updated. To force your app to update the subscriptions, uninstall and reinstall the app. Revisiting the app will call the `afterAuth` hook.
   168→
   169→### Webhooks: Admin created webhook failing HMAC validation
   170→
   171→Webhooks subscriptions created in the [Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/orders/notifications/webhooks) will fail HMAC validation. This is because the webhook payload is not signed with your app's secret key.
   172→
   173→The recommended solution is to use [app-specific webhooks](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe#app-specific-subscriptions) defined in your toml file instead. Test your webhooks by triggering events manually in the Shopify admin(e.g. Updating the product title to trigger a `PRODUCTS_UPDATE`).
   174→
   175→### Webhooks: Admin object undefined on webhook events triggered by the CLI
   176→
   177→When you trigger a webhook event using the Shopify CLI, the `admin` object will be `undefined`. This is because the CLI triggers an event with a valid, but non-existent, shop. The `admin` object is only available when the webhook is triggered by a shop that has installed the app. This is expected.
   178→
   179→Webhooks triggered by the CLI are intended for initial experimentation testing of your webhook configuration. For more information on how to test your webhooks, see the [Shopify CLI documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/commands#webhook-trigger).
   180→
   181→### Incorrect GraphQL Hints
   182→
   183→By default the [graphql.vscode-graphql](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GraphQL.vscode-graphql) extension for will assume that GraphQL queries or mutations are for the [Shopify Admin API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin). This is a sensible default, but it may not be true if:
   184→
   185→1. You use another Shopify API such as the storefront API.
   186→2. You use a third party GraphQL API.
   187→
   188→If so, please update [.graphqlrc.ts](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/.graphqlrc.ts).
   189→
   190→### Using Defer & await for streaming responses
   191→
   192→By default the CLI uses a cloudflare tunnel. Unfortunately cloudflare tunnels wait for the Response stream to finish, then sends one chunk. This will not affect production.
   193→
   194→To test [streaming using await](https://reactrouter.com/api/components/Await#await) during local development we recommend [localhost based development](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/cli-for-apps/networking-options#localhost-based-development).
   195→
   196→### "nbf" claim timestamp check failed
   197→
   198→This is because a JWT token is expired. If you are consistently getting this error, it could be that the clock on your machine is not in sync with the server. To fix this ensure you have enabled "Set time and date automatically" in the "Date and Time" settings on your computer.
   199→
   200→### Using MongoDB and Prisma
   201→
   202→If you choose to use MongoDB with Prisma, there are some gotchas in Prisma's MongoDB support to be aware of. Please see the [Prisma SessionStorage README](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shopify/shopify-app-session-storage-prisma#mongodb).
   203→
   204→### Unable to require(`C:\...\query_engine-windows.dll.node`).
   205→
   206→Unable to require(`C:\...\query_engine-windows.dll.node`).
   207→The Prisma engines do not seem to be compatible with your system.
   208→
   209→query_engine-windows.dll.node is not a valid Win32 application.
   210→
   211→**Fix:** Set the environment variable:
   212→
   213→```shell
   214→PRISMA_CLIENT_ENGINE_TYPE=binary
   215→```
   216→
   217→This forces Prisma to use the binary engine mode, which runs the query engine as a separate process and can work via emulation on Windows ARM64.

# Shopify App Template - React Router

This is a template for building a [Shopify app](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/getting-started) using [React Router](https://reactrouter.com/). It was forked from the [Shopify Remix app template](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix) and converted to React Router.

Rather than cloning this repo, follow the [Quick Start steps](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router#quick-start).

Visit the [`shopify.dev` documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) for more details on the React Router app package.

## Upgrading from Remix

If you have an existing Remix app that you want to upgrade to React Router, please follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/wiki/Upgrading-from-Remix). Otherwise, please follow the quick start guide below.

## Quick start

### Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need to [download and install the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/getting-started) if you haven't already.

### Setup

```shell
shopify app init --template=https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router
```

### Local Development

```shell
shopify app dev
```

Press P to open the URL to your app. Once you click install, you can start development.

Local development is powered by [the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli). It logs into your account, connects to an app, provides environment variables, updates remote config, creates a tunnel and provides commands to generate extensions.

### Authenticating and querying data

To authenticate and query data you can use the `shopify` const that is exported from `/app/shopify.server.js`:

# Learn more about configuring your app at https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/configuration

client_id = "0f048c328463b2e5d4659735a126703d"
name = "Zip Code Checker"
application_url = "https://automatic-palm-tree-q7rgr65prq672x9p6-4040.app.github.dev"
embedded = true

[build]
automatically_update_urls_on_dev = true
include_config_on_deploy = true

[webhooks]
api_version = "2026-01"

  [[webhooks.subscriptions]]
  topics = [ "app/scopes_update" ]
  uri = "/webhooks/app/scopes_update"

  [[webhooks.subscriptions]]
  topics = [ "app/uninstalled" ]
  uri = "/webhooks/app/uninstalled"

  [[webhooks.subscriptions]]
  topics = [ "app_subscriptions/update" ]
  uri = "/webhooks/app_subscriptions/update"

[access_scopes]
# Learn more at https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/configuration#access_scopes
scopes = "write_products,write_metaobject_definitions,write_metaobjects"
optional_scopes = []
use_legacy_install_flow = false

[auth]
redirect_urls = [ "https://automatic-palm-tree-q7rgr65prq672x9p6-4040.app.github.dev/auth/callback" ]

[product.metafields.app.demo_info]
type = "single_line_text_field"
name = "Demo Source Info"
description = "Tracks products created by the Shopify app template for development"

  [product.metafields.app.demo_info.access]
  admin = "merchant_read_write"

[metaobjects.app.example]
name = "Example"
description = "An example metaobject definition created by this template"

  [metaobjects.app.example.access]
  admin = "merchant_read_write"

[metaobjects.app.example.fields.title]
name = "Title"
type = "single_line_text_field"
required = true

[metaobjects.app.example.fields.description]
name = "Description"
type = "multi_line_text_field"

  userId               BigInt?
  firstName            String?
  lastName             String?
  email                String?
  accountOwner         Boolean?
  locale               String?
  collaborator         Boolean?
  emailVerified        Boolean?
  refreshToken         String?
  refreshTokenExpires  DateTime?
}

model ZipCode {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop      String
  zipCode   String
  label     String?
  zone      String?
  message   String?
  eta       String?
  type      String   @default("allowed")
  isActive  Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@unique([shop, zipCode])
}

model DeliveryRule {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop          String
  name          String
  zone          String?
  zipCodes      String?  // comma-separated zip codes, or empty for "all in zone"
  minOrderAmount Float?
  deliveryFee   Float?
  freeShippingAbove Float?
  estimatedDays String?
  cutoffTime    String?  // e.g. "14:00" — orders after this go next day
  daysOfWeek    String?  // e.g. "Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri"
  isActive      Boolean  @default(true)
  priority      Int      @default(0)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([shop])
}

model WaitlistEntry {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop      String
  email     String
  zipCode   String
  note      String?
  status    String   @default("waiting") // waiting, notified, converted
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@unique([shop, email, zipCode])
  @@index([shop])
}

model WidgetConfig {
  id                    String  @id @default(cuid())
  shop                  String  @unique
  // Layout
  position              String  @default("inline") // inline, floating, popup
  // Colors
  primaryColor          String  @default("#008060")
  successColor          String  @default("#008060")
  errorColor            String  @default("#D72C0D")
  backgroundColor       String  @default("#FFFFFF")
  textColor             String  @default("#202223")
  // Text
  heading               String  @default("Check Delivery Availability")
  placeholder           String  @default("Enter your zip code")
  buttonText            String  @default("Check")
  successMessage        String  @default("Great news! We deliver to your area.")
  errorMessage          String  @default("Sorry, we don't deliver to this area yet.")
  notFoundMessage       String  @default("This zip code was not found in our system.")
  // Features
  showEta               Boolean @default(true)
  showZone              Boolean @default(false)
  showWaitlistOnFailure Boolean @default(false)
  // Border
  borderRadius          String  @default("8")
  // Custom CSS
  customCss             String?

  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

model Subscription {
  id                    String    @id @default(cuid())
  shop                  String    @unique
  planId                String    @default("free")
  billingInterval       String    @default("monthly")
  shopifySubscriptionId String?
  status                String    @default("active")
  trialEndsAt           DateTime?
  createdAt             DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime  @updatedAt
}

Now I have a thorough understanding of the codebase. Let me now create a comprehensive plan for restructuring this into a production-grade Shopify app. Let me also check a few more files to get the complete picture.

Key findings so far:
1. **Template leftovers to remove:**
   - `app/routes/app.additional.tsx` - This is a template "About" page with generic content, links to Shopify docs for developers. Not a user-facing page. Should be removed or repurposed.
   - `shopify.app.toml` has template demo metafield `[product.metafields.app.demo_info]` with "Demo Source Info" and description "Tracks products created by the Shopify app template for development" - this is a template artifact and needs to be removed
   - There's also an example metaobject definition in `shopify.app.toml` that's just a template placeholder and should be deleted
   - `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md` are template boilerplate that need to be replaced with app-specific content
   - The `package.json` author field is set to "codespace" and needs updating

2. **Production issues:**
   - The app is currently using SQLite (`prisma/dev.db`) which won't work in production—I need to migrate to PostgreSQL
   - The `.env` file has a local database path that needs to be replaced with a proper production database URL
   - The application configuration needs additional production setup

3. **Access scopes issue:**
   - The current scopes (`write_products`, `write_metaobject_definitions`, `write_metaobjects`) are overly permissive for what this app actually does
   - Looking at the codebase, the app stores zip codes in its own database rather than using Shopify's API, so these scopes aren't even being used and should be trimmed down

4. **Missing features:**
   - CSV bulk import/export functionality is marked as coming soon but not implemented
   - The storefront widget integration has configuration in place but the actual implementation is incomplete

5. **Developer artifacts that need cleanup:**
   - The About page is template boilerplate with Shopify docs links and Polaris component references - it's not user-facing and should be replaced with actual app documentation
   - `shopify.web.toml` appears to be an unusual file for a standard Shopify app setup
   - The `@shopify/plugin-cloudflare` dependency in trustedDependencies looks like a template leftover since this is a Node.js app, not Cloudflare Workers
   - Prisma is listed in devDependencies but `@prisma/client` should be in regular dependencies for production use
   - The package.json author field is just a placeholder that needs updating

6. **Files and directories that shouldn't be committed:**
   - `.env` contains real API keys and must be removed
   - `prisma/dev.db` is a local SQLite database file
   - The `build/` directory is generated output
   - The `.shopify/` directory should already be in gitignore

7. **Routes and configuration:**
   - The `app.additional.tsx` route is the default template page name and isn't even linked in the main nav - it should either be removed or replaced with proper documentation
   - `shopify.web.toml` is actually necessary as the React Router framework configuration
   - Need to check what `globals.d.ts` contains

Now I'm thinking through what needs to change for production. There are several structural issues: the shopify.app.toml still has demo metafield and metaobject configurations, the database is SQLite when it should be PostgreSQL, the access scopes might be too broad, and `@prisma/client` is incorrectly listed as a dev dependency. The app.tsx navigation doesn't link to the additional page, making it unreachable, and there's no public API endpoint for the storefront widget even though the widget is configured. On the positive side, the overall structure is sound.

The app already has good foundations—it follows Shopify's React Router template, billing is integrated properly, webhooks are configured, session storage uses Prisma, TypeScript is enabled, and the authentication flow is correct. For Shopify App Store approval, I need to ensure all mandatory webhooks are handled (app/uninstalled and app/scopes_update), implement GDPR compliance with data deletion webhooks (customers/data_request, customers/redact, shop/redact), add proper error handling, avoid over-requesting scopes, use HTTPS for the application URL, and pass Shopify's automated checks. There's also the requirement for privacy policy and terms of service, though those live outside the app itself.

Looking at what's actually missing, the GDPR webhooks are critical—Shopify requires these for any app in the App Store to handle customer data requests and deletion across all three scenarios. I should also audit the scopes being requested since write_products doesn't appear to be used, and the zip code data is stored in the app's own database rather than in Shopify metaobjects, so some of those scope requests might be unnecessary.

For cleanup, I need to remove the unused additional page template, strip out the demo metafield and metaobject configuration, and add proper gitignore rules. On the implementation side, I'll need to create the GDPR webhook handlers, expose a public API endpoint for the storefront widget to validate zip codes, and fix the package.json by moving Prisma to dependencies and updating the author field.

Now I'm reviewing the shopify.app.toml configuration to remove the template demo entries and add the required GDPR subscriptions, plus trim back the access scopes to only what's actually needed.

# Production-Grade Shopify App Restructure Plan

## Context
The app is a Shopify Zip Code Checker (React Router 7 + Polaris + Prisma + SQLite).
It was bootstrapped from the official Shopify app template but still contains
template leftovers, is missing Shopify App Store mandatory GDPR webhooks, has
over-privileged OAuth scopes, and has a broken .gitignore for its SQLite file.
Goal: clean up all template artifacts, add missing mandatory compliance items,
fix dependency classification errors, and make the app submission-ready.

---

## Full File/Folder Audit

### Current Structure (clean — keep as-is)
```
app/
  billing.server.ts       ✅ billing logic
  db.server.ts            ✅ Prisma singleton
  entry.server.tsx        ✅ SSR entry
  globals.d.ts            ✅ global type declarations
  plans.ts                ✅ plan constants & limits
  root.tsx                ✅ HTML shell
  routes.ts               ✅ React Router route manifest
  shopify.server.ts       ✅ Shopify app init + billing config
  routes/
    app.tsx               ✅ layout + nav (Polaris + AppProvider)
    app._index.tsx        ✅ Dashboard
    app.zip-codes.tsx     ✅ Zip code manager
    app.delivery-rules.tsx ✅ Delivery rules
    app.waitlist.tsx      ✅ Customer waitlist
    app.widget.tsx        ✅ Widget customisation
    app.settings.tsx      ✅ Settings & billing
    app.pricing.tsx       ✅ Pricing / upgrade
    auth.$.tsx            ✅ OAuth catch-all
    auth.login/           ✅ Login page
    webhooks.app.scopes_update.tsx      ✅ Mandatory
    webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx        ✅ Mandatory
    webhooks.app_subscriptions.update.tsx ✅ Billing
    _index/route.tsx      ✅ Public landing page
    _index/styles.module.css ✅ Landing styles
prisma/
  schema.prisma           ✅ DB schema (SQLite → PostgreSQL needed for prod)
  migrations/             ✅ Migration history
  dev.db                  ⚠️  Should NOT be committed (gitignore bug)
public/
  favicon.ico             ✅
shopify.app.toml          ⚠️  Has template demo artifacts
shopify.web.toml          ✅ React Router web framework config
vite.config.ts            ✅
tsconfig.json             ✅
package.json              ⚠️  @prisma/client in devDeps, wrong author
.gitignore                ⚠️  Missing prisma/dev.db entry
Dockerfile                ✅
env.d.ts                  ✅
CHANGELOG.md              ⚠️  Generic template changelog — wipe/replace
README.md                 ⚠️  Generic template README — wipe/replace
```

### Files to DELETE
| File | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `app/routes/app.additional.tsx` | Template boilerplate "About" page with links to Shopify dev docs. Not in the nav. No real user value. Should be removed entirely. |

### No unwanted folders found
All directories serve a purpose. `extensions/` with `.gitkeep` is correct — Shopify CLI requires it for workspace configuration.

---

## Issues & Required Changes

### 1. CRITICAL — Missing GDPR Mandatory Webhooks
Shopify **requires** these 3 webhooks for any App Store submission. Without them the app will be rejected during review.

**Add these 3 new route files:**
- `app/routes/webhooks.customers.data_request.tsx`
- `app/routes/webhooks.customers.redact.tsx`
- `app/routes/webhooks.shop.redact.tsx`

**Update `shopify.app.toml`** to register them:
```toml
[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
topics = [ "customers/data_request" ]
uri = "/webhooks/customers/data_request"

[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
topics = [ "customers/redact" ]
uri = "/webhooks/customers/redact"

[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
topics = [ "shop/redact" ]
uri = "/webhooks/shop/redact"
```

### 2. CRITICAL — Template Demo Artifacts in shopify.app.toml
The `shopify.app.toml` contains two sections that are copy-pasted from the Shopify app template and have nothing to do with a Zip Code Checker:

**Remove entirely:**
```toml
[product.metafields.app.demo_info]   ← "Demo Source Info / Tracks products created by the Shopify app template"
[metaobjects.app.example]            ← "An example metaobject definition created by this template"
```
These create unnecessary metafield/metaobject definitions in every merchant's store.

### 3. CRITICAL — Over-Privileged OAuth Scopes
Current scopes: `write_products, write_metaobject_definitions, write_metaobjects`

The entire app stores data in its **own** Prisma database — no Shopify API calls to products or metaobjects exist anywhere in the codebase. These scopes are completely unused.

Shopify's app review will flag over-privileged scopes as a policy violation.

**Fix in `shopify.app.toml`:**
```toml
[access_scopes]
scopes = ""    # or remove line entirely; app needs no Shopify data scopes
```
If the storefront widget public API is added (see #6), it needs no scopes either.

### 4. IMPORTANT — .gitignore Missing dev.db Entry
Current `.gitignore` has `prisma/dev.sqlite` but the actual database file is `prisma/dev.db`. This means **dev.db is currently committed to git**, which is a security/data risk.

**Fix `.gitignore`:**
```
prisma/dev.db
prisma/dev.db-journal
prisma/*.db
prisma/*.db-journal
```

### 5. IMPORTANT — @prisma/client in devDependencies
`@prisma/client` is in `devDependencies` but is required at **runtime** in production (imported by `db.server.ts`). The Docker/production build will fail without it in `dependencies`.

**Fix `package.json`:** move `@prisma/client` from `devDependencies` → `dependencies`.

### 6. IMPORTANT — No Public API Endpoint for Storefront Widget
The app has a full `WidgetConfig` model and widget customisation UI, but there is **no public API route** for the storefront to actually check zip codes. Without this, the widget cannot function.

**Add:** `app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` — unauthenticated GET/POST endpoint:
- Accepts: `?shop=store.myshopify.com&zip=12345`
- Returns: JSON `{ allowed: true/false, message, eta, zone }`
- Uses `unauthenticated.public` from shopify.server
- Enforces CORS headers for storefront cross-origin requests

### 7. MINOR — Template Artifacts in package.json
- `"author": "codespace"` → update to real author/company name
- `@shopify/plugin-cloudflare` in `trustedDependencies` → template artifact, this app uses Node.js/Docker not Cloudflare; remove it

### 8. MINOR — API Version Inconsistency
- `shopify.app.toml` webhooks: `api_version = "2026-01"`
- `shopify.server.ts`: `ApiVersion.October25` (= `2025-10`)

**Fix:** Align both to `2026-01` / `ApiVersion.January26` in `shopify.server.ts`.

### 9. MINOR — Template CHANGELOG.md & README.md
Both files contain generic Shopify template boilerplate. Replace with app-specific content describing Zip Code Checker.

---

## Summary of All Changes

### DELETE (1 file)
- `app/routes/app.additional.tsx`

### MODIFY (5 files)
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `shopify.app.toml` | Remove demo metafield + example metaobject; remove unused scopes; add 3 GDPR webhook subscriptions |
| `package.json` | Move `@prisma/client` to dependencies; update author; remove cloudflare trustedDependency |
| `.gitignore` | Add `prisma/dev.db` and `prisma/*.db-journal` |
| `app/shopify.server.ts` | Align API version to January26 (2026-01) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` / `README.md` | Replace with app-specific content |

### ADD (4 files)
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/routes/webhooks.customers.data_request.tsx` | GDPR: customer data request (mandatory for App Store) |
| `app/routes/webhooks.customers.redact.tsx` | GDPR: customer data deletion (mandatory for App Store) |
| `app/routes/webhooks.shop.redact.tsx` | GDPR: shop data deletion after uninstall (mandatory for App Store) |
| `app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` | Public API for storefront widget zip lookup |

---

## Production Database Note
SQLite is fine for development but NOT for production (no concurrent writes, single file).
For App Store deployment, migrate to **PostgreSQL**:
- Change `prisma/schema.prisma` provider from `sqlite` → `postgresql`
- Set `DATABASE_URL` to a real Postgres connection string
- Run `prisma migrate deploy`
This is a deployment config change, not a code change.

---

## Verification Steps
1. `npm run typecheck` — should pass with no errors after all changes
2. `npm run lint` — no linting errors
3. `npm run dev` — app starts, dashboard loads, nav works (no /additional link should be accessible)
4. Verify GDPR webhooks are registered in Shopify Partners dashboard after `shopify app deploy`
5. Verify access scopes show correctly in Partners dashboard (no product/metaobject scopes)
6. Test public API: `GET /api/zip-check?shop=test.myshopify.com&zip=12345` returns JSON
7. Shopify App Store pre-submission checklist: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/app-requirements

    webhooks.app_subscriptions.update.tsx ✅ Billing
    _index/route.tsx      ✅ Public landing page
    _index/styles.module.css ✅ Landing styles
prisma/
  schema.prisma           ✅ DB schema (SQLite → PostgreSQL needed for prod)
  migrations/             ✅ Migration history
  dev.db                  ⚠️  Should NOT be committed (gitignore bug)
public/
  favicon.ico             ✅
shopify.app.toml          ⚠️  Has template demo artifacts
shopify.web.toml          ✅ React Router web framework config
vite.config.ts            ✅
tsconfig.json             ✅
package.json              ⚠️  @prisma/client in devDeps, wrong author
.gitignore                ⚠️  Missing prisma/dev.db entry
Dockerfile                ✅
env.d.ts                  ✅
CHANGELOG.md              ⚠️  Generic template changelog — wipe/replace
README.md                 ⚠️  Generic template README — wipe/replace
```

### Files to DELETE
| File | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `app/routes/app.additional.tsx` | Template boilerplate "About" page with links to Shopify dev docs. Not in the nav. No real user value. Should be removed entirely. |

### No unwanted folders found
All directories serve a purpose. `extensions/` with `.gitkeep` is correct — Shopify CLI requires it for workspace configuration.

---

## Issues & Required Changes

### 1. CRITICAL — Missing GDPR Mandatory Webhooks
Shopify **requires** these 3 webhooks for any App Store submission. Without them the app will be rejected during review.

**Add these 3 new route files:**
- `app/routes/webhooks.customers.data_request.tsx`
- `app/routes/webhooks.customers.redact.tsx`
- `app/routes/webhooks.shop.redact.tsx`

**Update `shopify.app.toml`** to register them:
```toml
[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
topics = [ "customers/data_request" ]
uri = "/webhooks/customers/data_request"

[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
topics = [ "customers/redact" ]
uri = "/webhooks/customers/redact"

[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
topics = [ "shop/redact" ]
uri = "/webhooks/shop/redact"
```

### 2. CRITICAL — Template Demo Artifacts in shopify.app.toml
The `shopify.app.toml` contains two sections that are copy-pasted from the Shopify app template and have nothing to do with a Zip Code Checker:

**Remove entirely:**
```toml
[product.metafields.app.demo_info]   ← "Demo Source Info / Tracks products created by the Shopify app template"
[metaobjects.app.example]            ← "An example metaobject definition created by this template"
```
These create unnecessary metafield/metaobject definitions in every merchant's store.

### 3. CRITICAL — Over-Privileged OAuth Scopes
Current scopes: `write_products, write_metaobject_definitions, write_metaobjects`

The entire app stores data in its **own** Prisma database — no Shopify API calls to products or metaobjects exist anywhere in the codebase. These scopes are completely unused.

Shopify's app review will flag over-privileged scopes as a policy violation.

**Fix in `shopify.app.toml`:**
```toml
[access_scopes]
scopes = ""    # or remove line entirely; app needs no Shopify data scopes
```
If the storefront widget public API is added (see #6), it needs no scopes either.

### 4. IMPORTANT — .gitignore Missing dev.db Entry
Current `.gitignore` has `prisma/dev.sqlite` but the actual database file is `prisma/dev.db`. This means **dev.db is currently committed to git**, which is a security/data risk.

**Fix `.gitignore`:**
```
prisma/dev.db
prisma/dev.db-journal
prisma/*.db
prisma/*.db-journal
```

### 5. IMPORTANT — @prisma/client in devDependencies
`@prisma/client` is in `devDependencies` but is required at **runtime** in production (imported by `db.server.ts`). The Docker/production build will fail without it in `dependencies`.

**Fix `package.json`:** move `@prisma/client` from `devDependencies` → `dependencies`.

### 6. IMPORTANT — No Public API Endpoint for Storefront Widget
The app has a full `WidgetConfig` model and widget customisation UI, but there is **no public API route** for the storefront to actually check zip codes. Without this, the widget cannot function.

**Add:** `app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` — unauthenticated GET/POST endpoint:
- Accepts: `?shop=store.myshopify.com&zip=12345`
- Returns: JSON `{ allowed: true/false, message, eta, zone }`
- Uses `unauthenticated.public` from shopify.server
- Enforces CORS headers for storefront cross-origin requests

### 7. MINOR — Template Artifacts in package.json
- `"author": "codespace"` → update to real author/company name
- `@shopify/plugin-cloudflare` in `trustedDependencies` → template artifact, this app uses Node.js/Docker not Cloudflare; remove it

### 8. MINOR — API Version Inconsistency
- `shopify.app.toml` webhooks: `api_version = "2026-01"`
- `shopify.server.ts`: `ApiVersion.October25` (= `2025-10`)

**Fix:** Align both to `2026-01` / `ApiVersion.January26` in `shopify.server.ts`.

### 9. MINOR — Template CHANGELOG.md & README.md
Both files contain generic Shopify template boilerplate. Replace with app-specific content describing Zip Code Checker.

---

## Summary of All Changes

### DELETE (1 file)
- `app/routes/app.additional.tsx`

### MODIFY (5 files)
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `shopify.app.toml` | Remove demo metafield + example metaobject; remove unused scopes; add 3 GDPR webhook subscriptions |
| `package.json` | Move `@prisma/client` to dependencies; update author; remove cloudflare trustedDependency |
| `.gitignore` | Add `prisma/dev.db` and `prisma/*.db-journal` |
| `app/shopify.server.ts` | Align API version to January26 (2026-01) |
| `CHANGELOG.md` / `README.md` | Replace with app-specific content |

### ADD (4 files)
| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `app/routes/webhooks.customers.data_request.tsx` | GDPR: customer data request (mandatory for App Store) |
| `app/routes/webhooks.customers.redact.tsx` | GDPR: customer data deletion (mandatory for App Store) |
| `app/routes/webhooks.shop.redact.tsx` | GDPR: shop data deletion after uninstall (mandatory for App Store) |
| `app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` | Public API for storefront widget zip lookup |

---

## Production Database Note
SQLite is fine for development but NOT for production (no concurrent writes, single file).
For App Store deployment, migrate to **PostgreSQL**:
- Change `prisma/schema.prisma` provider from `sqlite` → `postgresql`
- Set `DATABASE_URL` to a real Postgres connection string
- Run `prisma migrate deploy`
This is a deployment config change, not a code change.

---

## Verification Steps
1. `npm run typecheck` — should pass with no errors after all changes
2. `npm run lint` — no linting errors
3. `npm run dev` — app starts, dashboard loads, nav works (no /additional link should be accessible)
4. Verify GDPR webhooks are registered in Shopify Partners dashboard after `shopify app deploy`
5. Verify access scopes show correctly in Partners dashboard (no product/metaobject scopes)
6. Test public API: `GET /api/zip-check?shop=test.myshopify.com&zip=12345` returns JSON
7. Shopify App Store pre-submission checklist: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/app-requirements

input.content:
# Zip Code Checker — Shopify App

A Shopify embedded app that lets merchants control delivery availability by zip code. Built with React Router 7, Shopify Polaris, and Prisma.

## Features

- **Zip Code Management** — Add, edit, activate/deactivate allowed and blocked zip codes
- **Delivery Zones & ETAs** — Group zip codes into zones with estimated delivery times
- **Delivery Rules** — Zone-based rules for fees, minimum order amounts, cutoff times, and schedules
- **Customer Waitlist** — Capture emails from unsupported areas and notify when coverage expands
- **Widget Customisation** — Style the storefront zip code checker widget without touching code
- **Billing** — Free, Pro, and Ultimate plans via Shopify App Subscriptions

## Tech Stack

- [React Router 7](https://reactrouter.com) (full-stack)
- [Shopify Polaris](https://polaris.shopify.com) v13
- [Shopify App React Router](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js)
- [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io) ORM (SQLite for dev, PostgreSQL for production)
- TypeScript, Vite

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Node.js ≥ 20.19
- A [Shopify Partner](https://partners.shopify.com) account and development store

### Setup

```bash
npm install
npm run setup        # prisma generate + migrate
npm run dev          # shopify app dev
```

### Scripts

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `npm run dev` | Start local dev server via Shopify CLI |
| `npm run build` | Build for production |
| `npm run start` | Serve the built app |
| `npm run setup` | Generate Prisma client and run migrations |
| `npm run deploy` | Deploy to Shopify |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript type checking |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |

## Production Database

Switch from SQLite to PostgreSQL for production:

1. Update `prisma/schema.prisma`:
   ```prisma
   datasource db {
     provider = "postgresql"
     url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
   }
   ```
2. Set `DATABASE_URL` to your PostgreSQL connection string
3. Run `npm run setup`

## Public API

The storefront widget calls a public endpoint to check zip code availability:

```
GET /api/zip-check?shop=store.myshopify.com&zip=12345
POST /api/zip-check  { "shop": "store.myshopify.com", "zip": "12345" }
```

Response:
```json
{ "allowed": true, "message": "We deliver to your area!", "eta": "2-3 days", "zone": "North" }
```

## GDPR Compliance

The app implements all three mandatory GDPR webhooks required by Shopify:

- `customers/data_request` — logs customer data requests for manual fulfilment
- `customers/redact` — deletes customer PII (waitlist entries)
- `shop/redact` — deletes all shop data 48 hours after uninstall

## Shopify App Store

This app is designed for submission to the Shopify App Store and follows all [Shopify app requirements](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/app-requirements).

# Zip Code Checker — Shopify App

A Shopify embedded app that lets merchants control delivery availability by zip code. Built with React Router 7, Shopify Polaris, and Prisma.

## Features

- **Zip Code Management** — Add, edit, activate/deactivate allowed and blocked zip codes
- **Delivery Zones & ETAs** — Group zip codes into zones with estimated delivery times
- **Delivery Rules** — Zone-based rules for fees, minimum order amounts, cutoff times, and schedules
- **Customer Waitlist** — Capture emails from unsupported areas and notify when coverage expands
- **Widget Customisation** — Style the storefront zip code checker widget without touching code
- **Billing** — Free, Pro, and Ultimate plans via Shopify App Subscriptions

## Tech Stack

- [React Router 7](https://reactrouter.com) (full-stack)
- [Shopify Polaris](https://polaris.shopify.com) v13
- [Shopify App React Router](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-js)
- [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io) ORM (SQLite for dev, PostgreSQL for production)
- TypeScript, Vite

## Development

### Prerequisites

- Node.js ≥ 20.19
- A [Shopify Partner](https://partners.shopify.com) account and development store

### Setup

```bash
npm install
npm run setup        # prisma generate + migrate
npm run dev          # shopify app dev
```

### Scripts

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `npm run dev` | Start local dev server via Shopify CLI |
| `npm run build` | Build for production |
| `npm run start` | Serve the built app |
| `npm run setup` | Generate Prisma client and run migrations |
| `npm run deploy` | Deploy to Shopify |
| `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript type checking |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |

## Production Database

Switch from SQLite to PostgreSQL for production:

1. Update `prisma/schema.prisma`:
   ```prisma
   datasource db {
     provider = "postgresql"
     url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
   }
   ```
2. Set `DATABASE_URL` to your PostgreSQL connection string
3. Run `npm run setup`

## Public API

The storefront widget calls a public endpoint to check zip code availability:

```
GET /api/zip-check?shop=store.myshopify.com&zip=12345
POST /api/zip-check  { "shop": "store.myshopify.com", "zip": "12345" }
```

Response:
```json
{ "allowed": true, "message": "We deliver to your area!", "eta": "2-3 days", "zone": "North" }
```

## GDPR Compliance

The app implements all three mandatory GDPR webhooks required by Shopify:

- `customers/data_request` — logs customer data requests for manual fulfilment
- `customers/redact` — deletes customer PII (waitlist entries)
- `shop/redact` — deletes all shop data 48 hours after uninstall

## Shopify App Store

This app is designed for submission to the Shopify App Store and follows all [Shopify app requirements](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/app-requirements).

# Shopify App Template - React Router

This is a template for building a [Shopify app](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/getting-started) using [React Router](https://reactrouter.com/). It was forked from the [Shopify Remix app template](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-remix) and converted to React Router.

Rather than cloning this repo, follow the [Quick Start steps](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router#quick-start).

Visit the [`shopify.dev` documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) for more details on the React Router app package.

## Upgrading from Remix

If you have an existing Remix app that you want to upgrade to React Router, please follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/wiki/Upgrading-from-Remix). Otherwise, please follow the quick start guide below.

## Quick start

### Prerequisites

Before you begin, you'll need to [download and install the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/getting-started) if you haven't already.

### Setup

```shell
shopify app init --template=https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router
```

### Local Development

```shell
shopify app dev
```

Press P to open the URL to your app. Once you click install, you can start development.

Local development is powered by [the Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli). It logs into your account, connects to an app, provides environment variables, updates remote config, creates a tunnel and provides commands to generate extensions.

### Authenticating and querying data

To authenticate and query data you can use the `shopify` const that is exported from `/app/shopify.server.js`:

```js
export async function loader({ request }) {
  const { admin } = await shopify.authenticate.admin(request);

  const response = await admin.graphql(`
    {
      products(first: 25) {
        nodes {
          title
          description
        }
      }
    }`);

  const {
    data: {
      products: { nodes },
    },
  } = await response.json();

  return nodes;
}
```

This template comes pre-configured with examples of:

1. Setting up your Shopify app in [/app/shopify.server.ts](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/shopify.server.ts)
2. Querying data using Graphql. Please see: [/app/routes/app.\_index.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/app._index.tsx).
3. Responding to webhooks. Please see [/app/routes/webhooks.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx).
4. Using metafields, metaobjects, and declarative custom data definitions. Please see [/app/routes/app.\_index.tsx](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/app/routes/app._index.tsx) and [shopify.app.toml](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/shopify.app.toml).

Please read the [documentation for @shopify/shopify-app-react-router](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/shopify-app-react-router) to see what other API's are available.

## Shopify Dev MCP

This template is configured with the Shopify Dev MCP. This instructs [Cursor](https://cursor.com/), [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) and [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and [Google Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) to use the Shopify Dev MCP.

For more information on the Shopify Dev MCP please read [the documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/devmcp).

## Deployment

### Application Storage

This template uses [Prisma](https://www.prisma.io/) to store session data, by default using an [SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/index.html) database.
The database is defined as a Prisma schema in `prisma/schema.prisma`.

This use of SQLite works in production if your app runs as a single instance.
The database that works best for you depends on the data your app needs and how it is queried.
Here’s a short list of databases providers that provide a free tier to get started:

| Database   | Type             | Hosters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| MySQL      | SQL              | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-mysql), [Planet Scale](https://planetscale.com/), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Google Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql) |
| PostgreSQL | SQL              | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-postgresql), [Amazon Aurora](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/aurora/), [Google Cloud SQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres)                                   |
| Redis      | Key-value        | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-redis), [Amazon MemoryDB](https://aws.amazon.com/memorydb/)                                                                                                        |
| MongoDB    | NoSQL / Document | [Digital Ocean](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/managed-databases-mongodb), [MongoDB Atlas](https://www.mongodb.com/atlas/database)                                                                                                  |

To use one of these, you can use a different [datasource provider](https://www.prisma.io/docs/reference/api-reference/prisma-schema-reference#datasource) in your `schema.prisma` file, or a different [SessionStorage adapter package](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-api-js/blob/main/packages/shopify-api/docs/guides/session-storage.md).

### Build

Build the app by running the command below with the package manager of your choice:

Using yarn:

```shell
yarn build
```

Using npm:

```shell
npm run build
```

Using pnpm:

```shell
pnpm run build
```

## Hosting

When you're ready to set up your app in production, you can follow [our deployment documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment) to host it externally. From there, you have a few options:

- [Google Cloud Run](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment/deploy-to-google-cloud-run): This tutorial is written specifically for this example repo, and is compatible with the extended steps included in the subsequent [**Build your app**](tutorial) in the **Getting started** docs. It is the most detailed tutorial for taking a React Router-based Shopify app and deploying it to production. It includes configuring permissions and secrets, setting up a production database, and even hosting your apps behind a load balancer across multiple regions.
- [Fly.io](https://fly.io/docs/js/shopify/): Leverages the Fly.io CLI to quickly launch Shopify apps to a single machine.
- [Render](https://render.com/docs/deploy-shopify-app): This tutorial guides you through using Docker to deploy and install apps on a Dev store.
- [Manual deployment guide](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/deployment/deploy-to-hosting-service): This resource provides general guidance on the requirements of deployment including environment variables, secrets, and persistent data.

When you reach the step for [setting up environment variables](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/deployment/web#set-env-vars), you also need to set the variable `NODE_ENV=production`.

## Gotchas / Troubleshooting

### Database tables don't exist

If you get an error like:

```
The table `main.Session` does not exist in the current database.
```

Create the database for Prisma. Run the `setup` script in `package.json` using `npm`, `yarn` or `pnpm`.

### Navigating/redirecting breaks an embedded app

Embedded apps must maintain the user session, which can be tricky inside an iFrame. To avoid issues:

1. Use `Link` from `react-router` or `@shopify/polaris`. Do not use `<a>`.
2. Use `redirect` returned from `authenticate.admin`. Do not use `redirect` from `react-router`
3. Use `useSubmit` from `react-router`.

This only applies if your app is embedded, which it will be by default.

### Webhooks: shop-specific webhook subscriptions aren't updated

If you are registering webhooks in the `afterAuth` hook, using `shopify.registerWebhooks`, you may find that your subscriptions aren't being updated.

Instead of using the `afterAuth` hook declare app-specific webhooks in the `shopify.app.toml` file. This approach is easier since Shopify will automatically sync changes every time you run `deploy` (e.g: `npm run deploy`). Please read these guides to understand more:

1. [app-specific vs shop-specific webhooks](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe#app-specific-subscriptions)
2. [Create a subscription tutorial](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe/get-started?deliveryMethod=https)

If you do need shop-specific webhooks, keep in mind that the package calls `afterAuth` in 2 scenarios:

- After installing the app
- When an access token expires

During normal development, the app won't need to re-authenticate most of the time, so shop-specific subscriptions aren't updated. To force your app to update the subscriptions, uninstall and reinstall the app. Revisiting the app will call the `afterAuth` hook.

### Webhooks: Admin created webhook failing HMAC validation

Webhooks subscriptions created in the [Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/orders/notifications/webhooks) will fail HMAC validation. This is because the webhook payload is not signed with your app's secret key.

The recommended solution is to use [app-specific webhooks](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/webhooks/subscribe#app-specific-subscriptions) defined in your toml file instead. Test your webhooks by triggering events manually in the Shopify admin(e.g. Updating the product title to trigger a `PRODUCTS_UPDATE`).

### Webhooks: Admin object undefined on webhook events triggered by the CLI

When you trigger a webhook event using the Shopify CLI, the `admin` object will be `undefined`. This is because the CLI triggers an event with a valid, but non-existent, shop. The `admin` object is only available when the webhook is triggered by a shop that has installed the app. This is expected.

Webhooks triggered by the CLI are intended for initial experimentation testing of your webhook configuration. For more information on how to test your webhooks, see the [Shopify CLI documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli/commands#webhook-trigger).

### Incorrect GraphQL Hints

By default the [graphql.vscode-graphql](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GraphQL.vscode-graphql) extension for will assume that GraphQL queries or mutations are for the [Shopify Admin API](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin). This is a sensible default, but it may not be true if:

1. You use another Shopify API such as the storefront API.
2. You use a third party GraphQL API.

If so, please update [.graphqlrc.ts](https://github.com/Shopify/shopify-app-template-react-router/blob/main/.graphqlrc.ts).

### Using Defer & await for streaming responses

By default the CLI uses a cloudflare tunnel. Unfortunately cloudflare tunnels wait for the Response stream to finish, then sends one chunk. This will not affect production.

To test [streaming using await](https://reactrouter.com/api/components/Await#await) during local development we recommend [localhost based development](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/cli-for-apps/networking-options#localhost-based-development).

### "nbf" claim timestamp check failed

This is because a JWT token is expired. If you are consistently getting this error, it could be that the clock on your machine is not in sync with the server. To fix this ensure you have enabled "Set time and date automatically" in the "Date and Time" settings on your computer.

### Using MongoDB and Prisma

If you choose to use MongoDB with Prisma, there are some gotchas in Prisma's MongoDB support to be aware of. Please see the [Prisma SessionStorage README](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shopify/shopify-app-session-storage-prisma#mongodb).

### Unable to require(`C:\...\query_engine-windows.dll.node`).

Unable to require(`C:\...\query_engine-windows.dll.node`).
The Prisma engines do not seem to be compatible with your system.

query_engine-windows.dll.node is not a valid Win32 application.

**Fix:** Set the environment variable:

```shell
PRISMA_CLIENT_ENGINE_TYPE=binary
```

This forces Prisma to use the binary engine mode, which runs the query engine as a separate process and can work via emulation on Windows ARM64.

- [React Router docs](https://reactrouter.com/home)

Shopify:

- [Intro to Shopify apps](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/getting-started)

- [Shopify CLI](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/tools/cli)
- [Shopify App Bridge](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-bridge-library).
- [Polaris Web Components](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/polaris-web-components).
- [App extensions](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/app-extensions/list)
- [Shopify Functions](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/functions)

## Smart Routing

Before diving in, classify the bug and route to the right agent:

| Bug type | Route to |
|---|---|
| TypeScript / build errors | **bug-fixer** agent |
| Runtime errors / crashes | **bug-fixer** agent |
| Auth / session issues | **bug-fixer** agent (Category A) |
| Prisma / DB errors | **bug-fixer** agent (Category D) |
| Shopify API errors | **bug-fixer** agent (Category E) |
| Webhook failures | **bug-fixer** agent (Category F) |
| Widget not rendering | **widget-specialist** agent |
| Public API returning wrong data | **widget-specialist** agent |
| CORS / CSP errors | **widget-specialist** agent |
| Polaris component visual bugs | **bug-fixer** agent (Category C) |
| Billing / subscription issues | **bug-fixer** agent (Category G) |
| Complex multi-system bug | Start with **bug-fixer**, hand off as needed |

## Debugging Process (Follow Exactly)

### Step 1 — Locate the Issue
- Find all files related to the error (route file, server file, Prisma schema)
- Read the FULL file where the error originates — understand context before changing anything
- Check the exact error message and stack trace
- Run `npm run typecheck` to see all TypeScript errors at once

### Step 2 — Classify Using Bug-Fixer Categories
Use the bug-fixer agent's diagnostic categories (A through G) to systematically check root causes. The most common:

**Auth issues (70% of Shopify bugs):**
- Is `authenticate.admin(request)` called before every Shopify API usage?
- Is `session.shop` being used to scope DB queries?
- Is the route missing auth (public routes `api.*` should NOT use admin auth)?

**TypeScript errors:**
- Run `npm run typecheck` to see all errors at once
- Check Prisma-generated types match usage
- Check React Router `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()` type inference
- React Router 7 imports from `react-router`, NOT `@remix-run/react`

**Polaris component errors:**
- Check Polaris v13 prop names — many changed from v12
- Check `.d.ts` files in `node_modules/@shopify/polaris/build/ts/src/components/`
- `Badge`/`Banner`: `status` → `tone` in v13

**Prisma/DB errors:**
- Check unique constraints: ZipCode `[shop, zipCode]`, WidgetConfig `shop`
- Use `upsert` for singleton records
- Run `npx prisma migrate dev` if schema changed without migration

**Webhook errors:**
- Must return 200 status always — even on internal errors
- Must be idempotent
- GDPR webhooks: `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`

### Step 3 — Read Before Fixing
Always read the full file before editing. Understand surrounding code context. Match existing patterns exactly.

### Step 4 — Fix (Minimal, Targeted)
- Fix ONLY what is broken — never refactor working code while fixing a bug
- If fixing a TypeScript error, don't change logic
- If fixing a logic bug, don't change types
- Make the smallest change that fixes the issue
- No `// @ts-ignore` or `as any` — fix the root cause

### Step 5 — Verify
- Run `npm run typecheck` — confirm ZERO errors (not just fewer)

content.text:
Zero errors. Here is the full diagnosis and what was fixed:

---

## What Was Wrong

### Bug 1 — HTML attribute single-quote breakage (Liquid block, all plans)

**File:** `extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`, line 104

```liquid
data-config='{{ zcc_config | json }}'
```

The attribute was delimited with single quotes. Shopify's `| json` filter serializes the widget config object to JSON, which is correct — but if any config field contains an apostrophe (the default `errorMessage` is `"Sorry, we don't deliver to this area yet."`, the default `errorMessage` in the DB), the literal apostrophe inside the JSON breaks the single-quoted HTML attribute. The browser parses the attribute value as only `{"errorMessage":"Sorry, we don` and the rest is treated as invalid HTML. `container.getAttribute("data-config")` then returns a truncated/broken string, `JSON.parse` throws in the catch block, and the widget falls back to the API fetch.

**Fix:** Changed to double-quote delimiters and added `| escape` to HTML-encode characters that would break the attribute:

```liquid
data-config="{{ zcc_config | json | escape }}"
```

This means the `'` in "don't" becomes `'` inside the attribute, which is safe. The JS `getAttribute` still receives the raw decoded string and `JSON.parse` works correctly.

### Bug 2 — Plan enforcement not applied in admin Live Preview (the root cause of the reported symptom)

**File:** `app/routes/app.widget.tsx` — `WidgetPreview` component

The admin Live Preview read colors directly from the form state (which mirrors the DB values) — no plan gating. The storefront API (`api.widget-config.tsx`) correctly enforces plan limits: when `widgetFullCustom` is `false` (Free plan), it resets `primaryColor`, `successColor`, `errorColor`, `backgroundColor`, and `textColor` back to defaults before responding.

This is exactly why the preview shows custom colors but the storefront does not — the admin preview was bypassing the same plan enforcement that the API applies.

**Fix:** Added a `widgetFullCustom` prop to `WidgetPreview`. When `false`, the component computes an `effectiveCfg` that mirrors what the API returns (colors reset to defaults, position reset to `inline`). All CSS generation and inline color values in JSX now use `effectiveCfg` instead of `cfg`. A `Banner` with tone `"warning"` is also shown above the preview frame to explain the discrepancy and link to the pricing page.

### Bug 3 — `backgroundColor` not applied to inline widget

**Files:** `extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid` and `app/routes/app.widget.tsx` — `buildWidgetCss`

The inline widget container had `background:transparent` hardcoded in both the storefront Liquid block and the admin preview's CSS generator. The `backgroundColor` config field only applied to the floating panel and popup modal. Merchants who set a custom background color saw no effect on the inline position.

**Fix:** Changed both `buildWidgetCss` functions to use `cfg.backgroundColor` on the widget container root element, so all three positions (inline, floating, popup) now apply the configured background color.

---

## Files Changed

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`
  - Line 104: attribute quoting fix (`'` → `"` + `| escape`)
  - `buildWidgetCss`: inline widget `background:transparent` → `background:" + cfg.backgroundColor + "`

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.widget.tsx`
  - `WidgetPreview`: added `widgetFullCustom` prop; computes `effectiveCfg` with plan-enforced defaults; all color/position usages switched to `effectiveCfg`
  - `buildWidgetCss`: inline widget `background:transparent` → `background:" + cfg.backgroundColor + "`
  - Live Preview section: added `Banner` warning when `!limits.widgetFullCustom` explaining that colors require Starter plan

Fix this issue in the Pinzo Shopify app: fix this bug any how in deep

/debug /review

## Smart Routing

Before diving in, classify the bug and route to the right agent:

| Bug type | Route to |
|---|---|
| TypeScript / build errors | **bug-fixer** agent |
| Runtime errors / crashes | **bug-fixer** agent |
| Auth / session issues | **bug-fixer** agent (Category A) |
| Prisma / DB errors | **bug-fixer** agent (Category D) |
| Shopify API errors | **bug-fixer** agent (Category E) |
| Webhook failures | **bug-fixer** agent (Category F) |
| Widget not rendering | **widget-specialist** agent |
| Public API returning wrong data | **widget-specialist** agent |
| CORS / CSP errors | **widget-specialist** agent |
| Polaris component visual bugs | **bug-fixer** agent (Category C) |
| Billing / subscription issues | **bug-fixer** agent (Category G) |
| Complex multi-system bug | Start with **bug-fixer**, hand off as needed |

## Debugging Process (Follow Exactly)

### Step 1 — Locate the Issue
- Find all files related to the error (route file, server file, Prisma schema)
- Read the FULL file where the error originates — understand context before changing anything
- Check the exact error message and stack trace
- Run `npm run typecheck` to see all TypeScript errors at once

### Step 2 — Classify Using Bug-Fixer Categories
Use the bug-fixer agent's diagnostic categories (A through G) to systematically check root causes. The most common:

**Auth issues (70% of Shopify bugs):**
- Is `authenticate.admin(request)` called before every Shopify API usage?
- Is `session.shop` being used to scope DB queries?
- Is the route missing auth (public routes `api.*` should NOT use admin auth)?

**TypeScript errors:**
- Run `npm run typecheck` to see all errors at once
- Check Prisma-generated types match usage
- Check React Router `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()` type inference
- React Router 7 imports from `react-router`, NOT `@remix-run/react`

**Polaris component errors:**
- Check Polaris v13 prop names — many changed from v12
- Check `.d.ts` files in `node_modules/@shopify/polaris/build/ts/src/components/`
- `Badge`/`Banner`: `status` → `tone` in v13

**Prisma/DB errors:**
- Check unique constraints: ZipCode `[shop, zipCode]`, WidgetConfig `shop`
- Use `upsert` for singleton records
- Run `npx prisma migrate dev` if schema changed without migration

**Webhook errors:**
- Must return 200 status always — even on internal errors
- Must be idempotent
- GDPR webhooks: `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`

### Step 3 — Read Before Fixing
Always read the full file before editing. Understand surrounding code context. Match existing patterns exactly.

### Step 4 — Fix (Minimal, Targeted)
- Fix ONLY what is broken — never refactor working code while fixing a bug
- If fixing a TypeScript error, don't change logic
- If fixing a logic bug, don't change types
- Make the smallest change that fixes the issue
- No `// @ts-ignore` or `as any` — fix the root cause

### Step 5 — Verify
- Run `npm run typecheck` — confirm ZERO errors (not just fewer)
- Confirm the fix does not break adjacent functionality
- For Prisma changes: check if migration is needed
- Verify auth scoping is intact

### Step 6 — Report
```
## Bug Fix Report
**Root cause**: [1 sentence]
**Category**: [A-G]
**Files changed**: [file:line_range for each]
**Fix applied**: [what changed and why]
**Verification**: `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors
**Follow-up needed**: [migration, env var, Shopify partner dashboard, or "none"]
**Recommended next**: Run `/review` to check for regressions
```

input.prompt:
CRITICAL BUG: The storefront ZIP code widget shows "Something went wrong. Please try again." when a customer enters a ZIP code and clicks Check. The widget renders correctly but the ZIP lookup fails every time.

App path: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code`

## What to investigate (in order):

### 1. Read these files fully first:
- `extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid` — the full storefront widget block
- `app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` — the public ZIP check API endpoint
- `app/routes/api.widget-config.tsx` — the public widget config API
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — check the ZipCode model unique constraint name
- `shopify.app.toml` — check if app_proxy is configured (important for API routing)

### 2. Key things to check:

**A. API URL construction in the widget JS:**
- What URL does the widget JS call when checking a ZIP? (`/api/zip-check`, `/apps/zipcheck/api/zip-check`, or something else?)
- Is it using the Shopify App Proxy URL (`/apps/zipcheck`) or the direct app URL?
- Is the `shop` parameter being passed correctly?
- Is there a CORS issue?

**B. The `shop_zipCode` unique constraint name in Prisma:**
- In `api.zip-check.tsx`, the code does `db.zipCode.findUnique({ where: { shop_zipCode: { shop, zipCode } } })`
- Check if the Prisma-generated constraint name is actually `shop_zipCode` or something different (in PostgreSQL it might be different). Check the actual generated Prisma client types.

**C. App Proxy configuration:**
- `shopify.app.toml` has `[app_proxy]` with `url`, `subpath = "zipcheck"`, `prefix = "apps"`
- This means the storefront calls `/apps/zipcheck/api/zip-check` and Shopify proxies it to `https://app-url/api/zip-check`
- The widget JS might be calling the wrong URL

**D. Error handling:**
- The widget shows "Something went wrong" — this is the catch block. What error is actually being thrown?
- Check if the API returns a non-200, or if JSON parsing fails, or if the fetch itself fails due to wrong URL

**E. `normalizeZipCode` utility:**
- `api.zip-check.tsx` imports `normalizeZipCode` from `../utils/zip` — does this file exist?
- If it doesn't exist, the API would crash on every request with a module not found error

**F. `shopSettings` model:**
- `api.zip-check.tsx` queries `db.shopSettings.findUnique(...)` — does the `ShopSettings` model exist in the deployed DB? Check if a migration was run.

### 3. Fix ALL issues found — don't stop at the first one. The "Something went wrong" could be caused by any of the above.

### 4. Run `npm run typecheck` and confirm zero errors.

### 5. Report ALL root causes found and all fixes applied.

content.text:
Zero errors. Here is the complete summary of every root cause found and every fix applied.

---

## Root Causes Found

### Root Cause 1 — Primary: `app.url` falling back to empty string breaks the API URL

**File:** `extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`, line 139 (original)

In Shopify Liquid, `{{ app.url }}` resolves to the App Proxy URL (e.g. `https://mystore.myshopify.com/apps/zipcheck`) **only when the app proxy is configured AND the theme extension is deployed to Shopify**. In a development environment, or when `app.url` returns a non-`http` value (empty string, relative path, or anything other than a full URL), the original code set `API_BASE = ""`.

With `API_BASE = ""`, the widget built the fetch URL as:
- `/api/zip-check?shop=...&zip=...`

On the storefront domain (`mystore.myshopify.com`), that path does not exist. Shopify returns a 404 HTML page. The widget's `r.json()` call on the HTML body throws a `SyntaxError`, which flows to the `.catch()` block, showing "Something went wrong."

### Root Cause 2 — Secondary: No console error logged, making the URL bug impossible to diagnose

The `.catch()` block received the error object but discarded it (`catch(function () { ... })`). There was no way to see in the browser console what URL was being called or what error occurred.

The `data.error` branch (line 524) similarly gave no diagnostic output.

---

## Fixes Applied

### Fix 1 — Robust `API_BASE` construction with proxy fallback

**File:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`

Added `data-proxy="/apps/zipcheck"` to the widget container `<div>` — a hardcoded fallback that matches `shopify.app.toml`'s `[app_proxy]` configuration (`prefix = "apps"`, `subpath = "zipcheck"`).

Changed the JS `API_BASE` assignment from:
```javascript
var API_BASE = (container.dataset.api || "").replace(/\/$/, "");
```
to:
```javascript
var _rawApi = (container.dataset.api || "").replace(/\/$/, "");
var _proxyPath = (container.dataset.proxy || "/apps/zipcheck").replace(/\/$/, "");
var API_BASE = (_rawApi && _rawApi.indexOf("http") === 0) ? _rawApi : _proxyPath;
```

This means:
- When `app.url` returns a full `https://` URL (the normal production case) — it uses that URL directly (same behavior as before)
- When `app.url` is empty, a relative path, or anything non-HTTP — it falls back to `/apps/zipcheck` which is the relative App Proxy path on the storefront. Shopify correctly forwards `/apps/zipcheck/api/zip-check` to the Railway app via the proxy.

### Fix 2 — Diagnostic console.error in `.catch()` block

Added `err` as a named parameter and `console.error('[ZipCodeChecker] ZIP check failed. API_BASE="..." SHOP="..."', err)` so the actual error, the API base URL, and the shop are visible in the browser console. This makes future debugging immediate.

### Fix 3 — Diagnostic console.error in `data.error` branch

Added `console.error('[ZipCodeChecker] API returned error:', data.error, ...)` in the `data.error && data.allowed === undefined` branch for the same reason.

---

## Files Modified

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`

## Files Investigated But No Changes Needed

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` — `normalizeZipCode` import is valid, `shop_zipCode` constraint name is correct, `ShopSettings` model exists in migrations, all response shapes match widget expectations
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/utils/zip.ts` — exists and is correct
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/prisma/schema.prisma` — `ShopSettings` model exists
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/shopify.app.toml` — App Proxy is correctly configured (`/apps/zipcheck` → Railway URL)
- `npm run typecheck` — zero errors before and after

## Next Step

After deploying the extension (`npx shopify app deploy`), open the storefront in a browser, open DevTools Console, enter a ZIP code and click Check. The `console.error` lines will now show the exact `API_BASE` value and `err` object being used — this will immediately confirm whether the proxy URL is correctly resolved. If you still see errors, the console output will pinpoint the exact URL being called.
